The maintenance division has 112 maintenance-worker positions. This year the city adopted several budget reductions, including a citywide hiring freeze from 6 January. Maintenance overtime for April–September is well over budget, and the council's Finance Committee wants an explanation and a corrective plan.

24	Presenting request: The Budget Office has asked you to explain the overtime overrun in the parks maintenance division and recommend what the department should do before the Finance Committee deadline of 15 December. Parks maintenance overtime for April–September totals $688,400, compared with $412,100 for the same months last year (+67%) and a budget of $430,000. Council's Finance Committee has asked for an explanation and corrective plan by 15 December. For reference, this year's adopted reductions for the department were: citywide hiring freeze on non-public-safety positions (from 6 January); deferral of two mower replacements ($118,000); non-renewal of the after-hours closing services contract ($96,000); reduced seasonal temp hours ($40,000). We started the year six maintenance workers short and we're at seventeen now. Every vacancy is a route somebody has to cover after their shift. July was brutal too, because the heat meant extra irrigation checks and mowing catch-up. I've asked the City Manager for an exemption to fill eleven positions; that brings overtime back to normal within a quarter.' 30	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dale Visconti, crew lead, Millbrook district, 5 November (staff-account): 'We're running routes two and three people short. He estimated he personally had worked 'about 25 hours of overtime a month' since April.

Allegation: two Riverside maintenance workers (named in the sealed record as Employees R-14 and R-22) 'are claiming night call-backs for parks they never go to. It's all paper slips, nobody checks. They're each pulling an extra grand a month.' Caller declined follow-up contact. Status: referred to Internal Audit for review on 26 August.

First, in Eastgate the night lock-ups keep going to the same handful of people the supervisor likes, and others never get asked. Second, if management answers this with an overtime cap, understand that members will stop taking call-backs, and then the gates and restrooms don't get locked. Nobody wants a repeat of the splash-pad break-in two years ago. Fill the vacancies and treat people fairly.

Title: Interview with the Eastgate district supervisor
Source: Interview notes, Marisol Adeyemi-Clark, Eastgate supervisor, 10 November (manager-account)

'I post a sign-up sheet every Monday for the week's closings. The same five or six people sign up most nights, because others have childcare or second jobs. If nobody signs, I direct the junior person, like the contract says. I don't keep the old sheets; they go in the bin when the week's over.' She said no one had told her about a complaint. She declined to estimate how call-backs were split among her 29 staff.

input.brief: The overtime rise is mostly call-back pay for nightly closing, not vacancies or heat. Since the Kestrel closing contract lapsed on 31 March, maintenance staff have been paid call-backs to lock 41 Riverside, Eastgate and Millbrook sites; Summit Hill, which kept its contract, shows no spike. The Internal Audit review also found the claims by the two flagged employees matched lock logs, so the hotline allegation is not supported. Regular overtime barely moved, so the freeze explains little of the step change. Confidence is good on the closing link, moderate on the rest. The Eastgate favoritism claim is unproven. Next steps: restore contracted closing (or an equivalent) for the 41 sites and track call-back spending. Do not impose a blanket overtime cap or discipline the two employees, since that would leave gates and restrooms unlocked. Review the 3-hour minimum for short closing rounds. Fill vacancies on their own merits. Check Eastgate call-back assignment fairly. Workers' compensation claims cannot yet be tied to overtime, because hours worked were not recorded.
